In time series forecasting, one can estimate the parameters of a forecasting model by using the observations at times 1, 2, ..., k to compute the errors on the forecast for k+1, k+2, ..., k+i. Repeat the above step for i = 2,...,T-k where T is the total number of observations. Compute the forecast accuracy over all errors. This procedure is sometimes known as a "rolling forecasting origin" because the "origin" (k+i -1) at which the forecast is based rolls forward in time. The Tyndale Bible, published in 1526, was the first English translation of the New Testament from the Greek. It was the work of William Tyndale, who translated directly from the Greek text rather than from the Latin Vulgate. The Tyndale Bible was the precursor to the King James Version and formed the basis for many of its translations.
